analysis.title: 2027 US Economics Outlook: Resilient Growth, Reluctant Disinflation
key_insights: Base case is resilient growth and reluctant disinflation. Real GDP grows 2.5% in 2027 and 2.7% in 2028 (4Q/4Q), driven by AI capex and wealth-supported upper-income consumers, without labor-market overheating.

Hyperscaler capex forecast is $1.6tn in 2027 and $1.8tn in 2028, up from $951bn in 2026. Growth decelerates from 98% in 2026 to 73% in 2027 and 7% in 2028. AI-related investment contributes 0.9pp to GDP growth in 2027, and the contribution is expected to peak in 2027.
Midterm outcome raises political risk for AI buildout. Equity analysts kept capex forecasts unchanged, but new governors could delay about 5GW of 2028 capacity in Texas and Ohio until 2029.

AI spending leaks heavily into imports (60-70% of hyperscaler capex goes to computers and peripherals, nearly all imported). Real imports grow 5.1% and 5.7% in 2027 and 2028 versus exports at 2.1% and 3.1%, so net trade drags GDP by about 0.6pp.

Consumption slows from 2.4% in 2026 to 2.0% in 2027, then 2.3% in 2028. Low- and middle-income households lead the slowdown as tax refunds and savings fade and OBBBA Medicaid/SNAP cuts bite. Household net wealth rose $20.6tn in four quarters and about 75% sits with the top income quintile, so asset markets drive consumption.

A Democratic midterm sweep could delay OBBBA Medicaid/SNAP cuts, adding up to 0.4pp to 2027 consumption in the Full Delay scenario (10bp in the Targeted Delay). Earliest legislative change is 1Q27, more realistically mid-2027 alongside debt ceiling talks.

Fiscal policy turns roughly neutral for growth in 2027 after a roughly 40bp boost in 2026. The deficit is forecast at 6.2% of GDP in 2026 and 5.9% in 2027, with upside risk from SNAP/Medicaid delays (up to $70bn). Debt limit is projected to bind in February 2027 with an x-date in late 3Q27.

Inflation falls reluctantly. Headline and core PCE slow to 2.3% and 2.6% 4Q/4Q in 2027 from 3.8% and 3.2% in 2026. Tariff payback (-30bp), airfares (-20bp), smaller AI boost (-10bp) and rents (-5bp) are offset by energy pass-through (+15bp) and healthcare (+5bp). Clear disinflation may not show until 2Q27 because of Q1 price-reset seasonality.

Labor market stays low-hire/low-fire. Payrolls average 35k per month in 2027 and 2028 versus a 50k breakeven, and unemployment drifts to 4.3% in 2027 and 4.4% in 2028. AI is estimated to add at most 15bp to unemployment, concentrated in young workers in exposed occupations.

Fed call: 25bp hikes in December and March to 4.25-4.50%, hold through 2027, then 75bp of cuts in 2028 to 3.5-3.75%. Risks skew to higher rates in the near term if inflation fails to decelerate or the labor market tightens, and lower if oil recedes or AI spending falters.

Real neutral rate estimate is about 150bp, midway between the 100bp (HLW) and 185bp (Lubik-Matthes) public estimates, implying a nominal neutral rate of 3.5% at 2% inflation. Wide confidence bands, and supply shocks may bias the estimate upward.

Warsh-led Fed is expected to cut communication and push balance sheet reform from 1Q-2Q27. Base case is about $1.5tn of reduction over two years (range $0.6-2.5tn) while keeping ample reserves, via tiered IORB, discount window collateral recognition, a smaller TGA, passive runoff and bill-heavy Treasury funding. Active MBS sales carry a 15% probability and could widen lower-coupon spreads 10-20bp.

Housing stays stuck. Rates strategists see the 10y at 5.0% at end-2027 and 4.75% at end-2028, with mortgage rates at or above 7% through 2027. Real residential investment is flat in 2027 and up 1.5% in 2028.

Trend productivity growth is 2.1% in 3Q26 (from 1.6% in 2019) and is expected to reach 2.3%. Gains come mainly from AI capital deepening in high-AI industries rather than broad diffusion. From 2028 the AI spending driver shifts from infrastructure to adoption (software).

Scenario probabilities: baseline 45%, aggregate demand upside 20% (Fed to 5.625%), AI slowdown 15% (unemployment 5.1%, Fed to 1.375%), productivity upside 10%, rates and oil downside 10% (oil $125-150, Fed to 5.375%, mild recession late 2027).

Reshoring evidence is limited. Supply chains are being rewired rather than reshored, and import penetration for all goods rose from about 25% in 2005 to about 33% in 2024. Computers and AI equipment show rising import dependence.

Higher rates are judged absorbable. FRB/US simulations show growth effects depend on the source of the rate rise, and a rise driven by stronger growth is far less damaging than one from tighter policy or term premium shocks.

sector_views.rationale: Capex forecast of $1.6tn in 2027 and $1.8tn in 2028 with returns above cost of capital, though growth decelerates to 7% in 2028 and political risks have risen.
Mortgage rates at or above 7% through 2027, strong lock-in, builder confidence at its lowest since 2012, and flat residential investment.
Goods spending leads the consumption slowdown, with tightening financial conditions hitting big-ticket purchases.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Solid growth led by AI capex, with 2.7% in 2028, supporting a hawkish-leaning Fed.
Down from a forecast 3.8% in 2026 on energy payback, still above 2% target.
Sticky, with 2.2% in 2028 and 3.2% tracked for 2026.
Two 25bp hikes in December and March, hold through 2027, then cuts to 3.5-3.75% in 2028.
Mild drift higher to 4.4% in 2028, no overheating.
Higher neutral rate limits room for easing.
6.2% in 2026 and 6.1% in 2028, deficits near 6% are the new norm.
Rates strategists expect 4.75% at end-2028, keeping mortgage rates at or above 7%.
Wage growth decelerating from 3.9% a year earlier.
Up from 0.84% in March, low single digit growth expected.
Down from 5.0% at end-2025, limited room to fall further.

risk_factors: Sharp AI spending pullback or lower AI profitability expectations triggering equity repricing and negative wealth effects (AI Slowdown scenario, 15%).
Oil spike to $125-150/bbl if Middle East conflict resolution fails, forcing Fed to hike to 5.375% and a mild recession in late 2027.
Labor market overheating from AI demand spillover would force a more aggressive Fed, up to 5.625%.
Political pushback, data center permitting delays, power and grid shortfalls could delay AI buildout.
Balance sheet reform done poorly could tighten financial conditions: active MBS sales, coupon-heavy Treasury funding, or scarce reserves raising repo volatility.
Debt ceiling binding in February 2027 with a late 3Q27 x-date.
Healthcare services inflation and broader energy pass-through could keep core inflation sticky.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict and the Iran war keep oil risk premium elevated, with Brent assumed near current levels through 2027 under a status-quo assumption.
Failure of the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding in early July 2026 kept oil disruption persistent and caused inflation to surprise to the upside.
Defense appropriations tied to the Iran war support government spending growth of 3.0% in 2027.
Strategic stockpiling, resource hoarding and supply chain reconfiguration reflect a multipolar world shifting from efficiency to resilience.
Tariffs persist with an effective tariff rate near 10%, IEEPA-related refunds distorted 2026 customs receipts.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are highly rated with returns far above cost of capital, so capex reaches $1.6tn in 2027 and $1.8tn in 2028 and supports wealth-driven consumption.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors fear debt- and equity-financed AI investment may not generate cash flows fast enough, and an abrupt slowdown would push unemployment to 5.1% and the Fed to 1.375%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A decline in the level of AI capital spending in 2027 and falling asset prices, as in the AI Slowdown scenario.

tension_points.bull_case: Measured recalibration with two 25bp hikes to 4.25-4.50% because the labor market shows few signs of overheating and payrolls run at 35k.
tension_points.bear_case: If labor demand accelerates and unemployment falls, the Fed hikes through 2027 to 5.625%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Unemployment falling toward 3.5% with firming wages and employment growth above 100k per month.
